Not connected. Create and launch an OpenCode session first: components will install automatically in Ubuntu. Then retry model selection or connection setup. Codex works independently.
OpenCode · Ubuntu. Select a connection for each session. Codex sign-in stays independent.

OpenCode stores the key locally in a separate connection. Saving does not check balance or model access and does not send an AI request. For your Codex subscription, choose Codex and use its normal sign-in.
Key saved. Model access is checked when you use the provider.
The catalog does not guarantee account access. Confirm the model and behavior before applying.
No saved OpenCode chats in this connection.
Permissions and sign-in appear in the OpenCode terminal. Account quotas are not calculated here.
A separate Ubuntu session will install OpenCode v2.0.28. Node.js 20+ and npm are required. Existing Codex is preserved.

OpenCode runs in Ubuntu. Create and launch checks components and installs them in this tab if needed. Node.js is installed separately from the system runtime. Connections and history are separate from Codex; permissions appear in the terminal.
First phase: Codex and OpenCode. This agent will be added after verification.
Close the session before changing its agent, connection or access level.
OpenCode history has not been created yet or the connection is unavailable. Save only the settings for a new chat?
Plan — analyze and prepare a plan. The mode does not replace access restrictions: choose Read only to prevent changes.
Build — implement tasks: file changes, builds and commands. Available actions depend on the access level.
Allowed tools may change files visible to Ubuntu and run commands without confirmation. This does not grant Android root or a separate sandbox. OpenCode policies may impose additional restrictions.
Reading, file search and questions are allowed. Editing, shell, subagents, MCP and unknown tools are denied by OpenCode rules. These are tool restrictions, not filesystem isolation.
OpenCode asks permission for actions. Choosing Allow always may save permission for the project. This mode does not create a filesystem sandbox.

OpenCode will reopen in this tab with the current chat history. The server and chat will stay alive. Unsent text inside OpenCode may be lost; the app input field stays unchanged. Model changes are unavailable during a response or while work is queued.
OpenCode is busy or has queued work. Wait for completion and try changing the model again.
Could not reopen OpenCode. Check the terminal; the selected model has not been confirmed.
Model changed; OpenCode is reopening with chat history
No open sessions. Create a new session.
Start OpenCode and wait for the connection first
Claude asks for action permissions in the terminal.
File edits and common filesystem commands are approved automatically; other actions require permission.
Analyze and plan without making changes. This is a Claude mode, not an operating system sandbox.

Claude Code runs in Ubuntu. Components are installed in a separate directory on first launch. A Claude subscription or paid API is required; ChatGPT Plus does not apply. Authentication and history are separate. Choose chat opens the Claude picker in the terminal. Model availability depends on your account.
This agent is not supported yet.

Model and permissions are set at launch. Current status: /status; change model: /model; permissions: /permissions; sign in: /login. Enter these commands in the Claude terminal. Claude saves its own history; choose a chat or enter its ID when starting again.
Gemini asks for action permissions in the terminal.
Gemini automatically approves editing tools; other actions require confirmation.
Analyze and plan without changes. This is a Gemini mode, not an operating system sandbox.

Gemini CLI runs in Ubuntu. Separate components are installed on first launch. To try the free tier, sign in with a personal Google account; availability depends on region and account. History is separate and tied to the project directory. Choose chat opens the terminal picker after sign-in. Select the original directory to resume.

This card shows Gemini launch settings. See the current model in the terminal; /model changes the model, /stats shows statistics, /auth opens sign-in, /resume opens history. Use the same project directory to continue. Free quotas depend on your account; live limits are not read here.
No Codex filesystem sandbox: files and commands are accessible within environment permissions, without approval prompts. This does not grant Android root.
Codex can edit project files and run commands inside its sandbox; leaving its boundaries requires approval. Sandbox support depends on Android/proot.
The Codex sandbox allows reading and inspection. Writing or exceeding restrictions requires approval. Sandbox support depends on Android/proot.
Sign in with Google only. Switching to an API key in this session is blocked; Google sign-in errors remain visible.
Sign in with a Gemini API key only. API terms and billing are separate from Google sign-in.
Native Gemini menu. Uses the sign-in method saved by the CLI; you can change it in the terminal.
Basic collection is automatic. Extended: events and error codes; Gemini also enables native debug at launch. No input or conversation recording. Changes apply on next launch.
Collected even while this window is closed. Updates automatically. Up to 2 MiB per session. Reports contain events and error codes, without conversations or secrets.
Cancel the following startup steps? All configured commands are listed below. The currently running command will continue.
